Section 1. Public workshop policy

Visitors may enter the public workshop between 08:00 and 18:00 on weekdays. Entry outside
those hours requires written permission from the duty manager and an escort trained for the
relevant room. Permission to enter does not authorize machinery use. The manager must record
the visitor name, arrival time, escort name and rooms visited, but must not collect a
visitor medical history.

Section 2. Public workshop policy

Members may borrow two portable tools for seven calendar days after completing the matching
safety course. A renewal is allowed once if no other member has reserved the tool. The
return deadline is extended until the next staffed opening when the workshop closes
unexpectedly. The borrower remains responsible for reporting damage and must not repair
electrical parts without written authorization.

Section 3. Public workshop policy

The workshop charges an annual membership fee of 120 credits and a refundable tool deposit
of 40 credits. Members with an approved hardship application pay 30 credits annually and no
deposit. Waivers apply prospectively from the approval date and do not erase earlier
assessed damage charges. Staff must issue an itemized receipt and keep disputed charges
separate from renewal fees.

Section 4. Public workshop policy

A member may cancel membership by sending written notice to the administrator. A
cancellation received within fourteen days of joining qualifies for a full refund only if no
tool has been borrowed and no training session attended. After that period, unused
membership time is not refundable. Deposits must be returned within twenty days after all
tools are returned, except for a documented amount needed to cover unresolved damage.

Section 5. Public workshop policy

The safety officer must inspect machine guards at the beginning of each staffed day and
immediately after reported interference. A missing or loose guard requires the affected
machine to be locked out until a qualified technician signs a repair record. Other machines
may remain available if the safety officer confirms they do not share the defective guard or
electrical isolation point. A member signature alone never authorizes reopening.

Section 6. Public workshop policy

Minors aged sixteen or seventeen may use hand tools only while a registered guardian or
designated instructor remains in the room. They may not operate saws, welders, presses or
powered cutting equipment. A school visit approval does not waive these restrictions. For
demonstrations, the instructor may operate a restricted machine while minors observe from
behind the marked barrier.

Section 7. Public workshop policy

The procurement committee must obtain three written quotations before purchasing equipment
costing more than 3000 credits. An emergency repair needed to restore fire protection may
proceed with one quotation when two committee members approve it in writing. The emergency
exception does not cover routine replacement or cosmetic work. The treasurer must publish
the supplier, price and reason for using the exception at the next monthly meeting.

Section 8. Public workshop policy

The treasurer must reconcile bank transactions every month and submit the reconciliation to
a trustee who did not authorize the payments. Cash reimbursements require a dated receipt
and the purpose of the expense. Missing receipts may be replaced only by a supplier
duplicate, not by the claimant own statement. A reimbursement exceeding 200 credits also
requires approval from a second trustee.

Section 9. Public workshop policy

The administrator may retain contact details while membership is active and for ninety days
after it ends. Incident records must be retained for three years, while payment records must
be retained for five years. Access is limited to staff whose duties require the particular
record. A member request to remove contact details does not require destruction of payment
or incident records before their retention period ends.

Section 10. Public workshop policy

A member may photograph a project only with consent from every identifiable person and the
project owner. Photographs of security controls, access codes or another member confidential
design are prohibited even if no person appears. An instructor may record a training
demonstration after announcing the recording and providing a camera-free alternative.
Recordings may not be reused for advertising without separate written consent.

Section 11. Public workshop policy

The workshop may suspend access immediately when a person presents an imminent safety risk.
The manager must provide written reasons within two working days and offer a hearing before
an uninvolved trustee within ten working days. Access remains suspended during review unless
that trustee grants a limited supervised visit. A complaint about fees alone does not
establish an imminent safety risk.

Section 12. Public workshop policy

The board meets quarterly and may decide ordinary matters when at least four trustees are
present. A trustee with a financial interest in a supplier must disclose it and leave the
discussion and vote about that supplier. The interested trustee does not count toward the
quorum for that decision. If the remaining trustees cannot form a quorum, the purchase must
be deferred or referred to a special member meeting.

donated equipment. The workshop may decline a donation without giving a reason. Acceptance

donor.

days. The administrator must send two notices at least seven days apart before moving

designs and may sell products they make unless a separate written commission transfers those
rights. A staff suggestion or use of workshop tools alone does not transfer design

workshop.

insurance valid for the event date. A free community demonstration may be exempted from the
insurance requirement by a trustee, but the named organizer and written booking remain
mandatory. Events serving food must separately comply with the kitchen cleaning and allergen
notice rules. Booking approval does not permit alcohol sales.

Complaints must be acknowledged within five working days. The investigator must give each
affected person an opportunity to respond and must not have participated in the disputed
decision. The written outcome must state the evidence considered, the decision and how to
appeal. Anonymous complaints may be investigated but cannot alone support permanent
expulsion without independently corroborated evidence.

Section 20. Public workshop policy

When flooding or severe weather makes the premises unsafe, the duty manager may close the
building immediately. Paid classes cancelled by the workshop must be rescheduled or refunded
at the participant choice. Membership periods are extended only when a closure lasts more
than seven consecutive days. Lost business income and travel expenses are not reimbursed
under this policy.

Section 21. Public workshop policy

The server backup runs nightly and must be checked weekly by the systems administrator.
Backup restoration must be tested quarterly using a separate test environment. Files
containing access codes must remain encrypted during transfer and storage. A successful
backup status alone does not count as a successful restoration test, and failed restoration
tests must be reported to the board within two working days.

Section 22. Public workshop policy

The accessibility coordinator must offer an alternative accessible workstation when a booked
station cannot be reached safely. A requested accommodation may change training format,
workstation height or appointment duration, but may not remove a machine guarding
requirement. The coordinator must discuss an alternative task if the requested activity
cannot be performed safely. Disability information must not appear on a publicly visible
booking calendar.

Section 23. Public workshop policy

The maintenance contractor must respond to urgent electrical faults within four hours and
routine faults within three working days. Replacement parts costing more than 500 credits
require written authorization before ordering. The response deadline measures
acknowledgement and initial assessment, not completion of a repair. The contractor must
state an estimated completion date after the assessment and update it when a required part
is unavailable.

Section 24. Public workshop policy

The annual report must include membership totals, training attendance, major purchases,
incident counts and approved policy changes. Names of injured members, medical details,
access codes and unresolved disciplinary allegations must be excluded. Financial totals must
distinguish income, refundable deposits and restricted grants. The report must be approved
by the board before publication and cannot describe an untested repair as certified safe.

clause_contexts.full_clause:
Section 5. Public workshop policy

The safety officer must inspect machine guards at the beginning of each staffed day and
immediately after reported interference. A missing or loose guard requires the affected
machine to be locked out until a qualified technician signs a repair record. Other machines
may remain available if the safety officer confirms they do not share the defective guard or
electrical isolation point. A member signature alone never authorizes reopening.

Section 6. Public workshop policy

Minors aged sixteen or seventeen may use hand tools only while a registered guardian or
designated instructor remains in the room. They may not operate saws, welders, presses or
powered cutting equipment. A school visit approval does not waive these restrictions. For
demonstrations, the instructor may operate a restricted machine while minors observe from
behind the marked barrier.

Section 7. Public workshop policy

The procurement committee must obtain three written quotations before purchasing equipment
costing more than 3000 credits. An emergency repair needed to restore fire protection may
proceed with one quotation when two committee members approve it in writing. The emergency
exception does not cover routine replacement or cosmetic work. The treasurer must publish
the supplier, price and reason for using the exception at the next monthly meeting.

Section 8. Public workshop policy

The treasurer must reconcile bank transactions every month and submit the reconciliation to
a trustee who did not authorize the payments. Cash reimbursements require a dated receipt
and the purpose of the expense. Missing receipts may be replaced only by a supplier
duplicate, not by the claimant own statement. A reimbursement exceeding 200 credits also
requires approval from a second trustee.
